title: English Vocabulary in Use — Pre-intermediate and Intermediate · Units 51–52

units.title: Unit 51 — Holidays by the sea
units.source: English Vocabulary in Use — Pre-intermediate and Intermediate (4th Edition); printed pages 108–109 (PDF pages 109–110).
units.bookTitle: English Vocabulary in Use — Pre-intermediate and Intermediate (4th Edition)
learningObjectives: Describe seaside settings, including beaches, waves, rocks, cliffs, sand and the shore.
Talk about water sports and common activities on a beach.
Distinguish calm and rough seas and recognise sun-related word families.
Use vocabulary for sun exposure, sun protection and risk correctly.
Use the everyday leisure patterns go for a walk, drive, swim or drink and have a swim, coffee or drink.

items.example: We spent the afternoon on a quiet beach.
items.note: An area of sand or stones beside the sea.

items.example: We stopped to admire the cliffs above the bay.
items.note: A high, steep face of rock beside the sea or elsewhere.

items.example: Small waves were breaking near the shore.
items.note: Moving ridges of water on the surface of the sea.

items.example: The children climbed over the rocks by the water.
items.note: A hard natural mass of stone.

items.example: There was fine white sand along the bay.
items.note: The small grains found on many beaches; normally uncountable.

items.example: They drove along the coast before reaching the hotel.
items.note: Land beside the sea.

items.example: The seaside resort is busy during the summer.
items.note: A town beside the sea where people go on holiday.

items.example: We found a sandy beach that was ideal for children.
items.note: Made of or covered with sand; compare rocky.

items.pt: dar uma caminhada tranquila; passear a pé
items.example: Shall we go for a stroll before dinner?
items.note: Stroll means a short, relaxed walk; go for a stroll is a fixed combination.

items.pt: faixa de terra junto à água; orla
items.example: A fisherman was standing on the shore.
items.note: The land at the edge of the sea or a lake.

items.pt: ao longo da orla; pela beira do mar
items.example: We walked along the shore at sunrise.
items.note: Along expresses movement following the edge of the water.

items.example: We enjoyed the warm sunshine all morning.
items.note: Direct light from the sun; an uncountable noun.

items.example: A cool breeze made the afternoon pleasant.
items.note: A gentle wind; stronger wind can be described simply as wind.

items.example: A gentle wind was blowing off the sea.
items.note: Blow off the sea indicates that the wind comes from the sea.

items.example: We played volleyball beside the water.
items.note: A sport in which two teams hit a ball over a net.

items.example: Do you want to play volleyball after lunch?
items.note: Use play with the name of this sport, without the.

items.example: Surfing is popular at this beach in winter.
items.note: Riding waves on a board.

items.example: She wants to try windsurfing during her holiday.
items.note: Moving on the water on a board with a sail.

items.example: They went diving to look at the fish.
items.note: Going underwater, especially as a sport or leisure activity.

items.pt: banho de sol; ato de tomar sol
items.example: Sunbathing for a long time can damage your skin.
items.note: Lying or sitting in the sun to become tanned; use sunbathe as the verb.

items.example: The hotel offers several water sports.
items.note: Sports done in or on water; often plural.

items.example: The calm sea was suitable for a gentle swim.
items.note: Calm describes water with little movement; opposite: rough.

items.example: We stayed out of the rough sea.
items.note: Rough describes the sea when there are large waves.

items.example: Let's go for a swim while the water is warm.
items.note: A common go for + noun pattern for leisure activities.

items.example: They like to lie on the beach and read.
items.note: Lie (lay, lain) means rest in a horizontal position; not lay something down.

items.example: He prefers to swim rather than sunbathe.
items.note: Verb related to the noun sunbathing.

items.example: She got a suntan while working outdoors.
items.note: A brown colour that the skin develops after exposure to the sun.

items.example: I get a suntan quickly in the summer.
items.note: A common verb–noun combination for skin becoming brown in the sun.

items.example: A hat can give you protection from the sun.
items.note: Something that keeps you safe; protection from something.

items.example: She had painful sunburn on her shoulders.
items.note: Red, sore skin caused by too much sun; uncountable in this use.

items.pt: sofrer queimadura solar; ficar queimado de sol
items.example: You can get sunburn even on a cloudy day.
items.note: Get sunburn is a natural phrase for developing sun-damaged skin.

items.pt: sob risco de; correndo o risco de
items.example: You are at risk of getting sunburn if you stay outside too long.
items.note: At risk of + noun or -ing form describes exposure to danger.

items.example: The article explains ways to reduce the risk of skin cancer.
items.note: A disease involving abnormal growth of skin cells.

items.example: Doctors recommend using sunscreen outside.
items.note: Often followed by a noun, -ing form or a that-clause; not usually recommend to do.

items.example: Remember to put on sunscreen before you go out.
items.note: A product put on the skin to protect it from ultraviolet light.

items.example: We bought sunblock at the shop near the beach.
items.note: Another word for a product that protects skin from the sun; usage varies.

items.example: Have you packed the sun cream?
items.note: British English expression for sunscreen.

items.example: The trees gave us some welcome shade.
items.note: A darker, cooler area sheltered from direct sunlight.

items.example: We sat in the shade during the hottest part of the day.
items.note: Use in the shade, not on the shade.

items.pt: sair para caminhar; dar uma caminhada
items.example: We went for a walk after breakfast.
items.note: Go for + a walk is a common leisure expression.

items.pt: sair para dar uma volta de carro
items.example: After lunch, we went for a drive through several coastal villages.
items.note: A drive can mean a car journey taken for pleasure.

items.example: We could go for a coffee after our walk.
items.note: This expression suggests going somewhere to drink coffee together.

items.example: Shall we go for a drink this evening?
items.note: A social invitation; drink often means an alcoholic drink in this context.

items.pt: dar um mergulho; nadar um pouco
items.example: We had a swim at the hotel pool before checking out.
items.note: Another common construction meaning swim for pleasure.

items.example: I had a coffee at the café near the beach.
items.note: A coffee can mean a cup of coffee.

items.example: We had a drink while we waited for our food.
items.note: A drink can refer to a serving of a beverage.

sectionsChecked: A: The beach; labelled coastal photograph, location descriptions and stroll, shore and breeze expressions
B: Beach activities; labelled sports images, water conditions, sun exposure and safety terms
Language help: go for and have with leisure activities
Exercises 51.1–51.6 and Unit 51 answer key; sun- word family, collocations, visual identification and contextual use

units.title: Unit 52 — Newspapers and television
units.source: English Vocabulary in Use — Pre-intermediate and Intermediate (4th Edition); printed pages 110–111 (PDF pages 111–112).
units.bookTitle: English Vocabulary in Use — Pre-intermediate and Intermediate (4th Edition)
learningObjectives: Recognise newspaper types, publishing frequency and digital editions.
Distinguish reports, articles, headlines, reviews and advertisements, including common prepositions.
Identify common television genres and words for media professionals.
Use channel for television and station for radio in the book’s examples.
Discuss online forums and podcasts, and report published news with according to and it says in the paper.

items.example: My grandfather reads the paper every morning.
items.note: Informal short form of newspaper; different from the material paper.

items.pt: diário; que ocorre todos os dias
items.example: She reads a daily newspaper on the train.
items.note: Daily means appearing or happening every day.

items.example: This local paper comes out every Friday.
items.note: Here come out means become available or be published, not physically leave a place.

items.example: The new edition will be published next month.
items.note: Passive form of publish; newspapers may also be published online.

items.example: The story appeared in a national newspaper.
items.note: Connected with or covering a whole country.

items.example: A regional paper reported the event first.
items.note: Connected with a part of a country, not the whole country.

items.pt: jornal digital; edição eletrônica de jornal
items.example: She reads the e-paper on her tablet.
items.note: Electronic edition of a newspaper.

items.example: The mobile edition is easy to read on a phone.
items.note: A version of a newspaper designed for mobile devices.

items.example: I bought a magazine about photography.
items.note: A publication containing articles and pictures, often weekly or monthly.

items.example: This is a weekly magazine about sport.
items.note: Appearing or happening once each week.

items.example: The organisation publishes a monthly magazine.
items.note: Appearing or happening once each month.

items.example: I read a report about the railway accident.
items.note: A factual account of a news event, often written by a reporter.

items.example: A reporter interviewed people outside the station.
items.note: Someone who gathers and reports news.

items.example: The journalist wrote an article about education.
items.note: A person who writes or presents news and other material for the media.

items.example: There is an interesting article about climate change.
items.note: A piece of writing on a subject in a newspaper or magazine.

items.example: The headline caught my attention immediately.
items.note: The prominent title above a news story.

items.example: I read a review of the new film.
items.note: A piece of writing that evaluates a book, film, product or performance.

items.example: An advertisement for a new phone filled half the page.
items.note: Publicity intended to encourage people to buy something.

items.example: I saw an advert for a language course.
items.note: Common British short form of advertisement.

items.pt: uma reportagem sobre; um relatório sobre
items.example: The newspaper published a report on local housing.
items.note: A report on/about a subject; both prepositions are possible.

items.pt: um artigo sobre; uma matéria sobre
items.example: Have you seen the article about electric vehicles?
items.note: The subject of an article can follow about or on.

items.pt: uma crítica de; uma resenha de
items.example: She wrote a review of the concert.
items.note: Use of to introduce the thing being reviewed.

items.pt: um anúncio de; um anúncio para
items.example: The website showed an advert for a new computer.
items.note: Use for to introduce the product or service advertised.

items.pt: transmitir por rádio, TV ou internet
items.example: The channel will broadcast the interview tonight.
items.note: Send programmes or information through TV, radio or the Internet.

items.example: The broadcasting company produces news programmes.
items.note: An organisation that produces or transmits radio or television programmes.

items.example: This programme starts at eight o'clock.
items.note: British spelling for a TV or radio show; American English usually uses program.

items.example: We watched the news before dinner.
items.note: Information about recent events, especially in a TV or radio programme.

items.example: The weather forecast says it will rain tomorrow.
items.note: A prediction of future weather.

items.example: I watched a documentary about the ocean.
items.note: A factual programme about real people, events or situations.

items.example: The actor appeared on a popular chat show.
items.note: A TV programme in which guests, often famous people, are interviewed.

items.example: We watched the whole series over the weekend.
items.note: A group of related episodes, with the same characters or subject; singular and plural forms are identical.

items.pt: novela; série dramática de longa duração
items.example: My grandmother watches a soap opera every evening.
items.note: A continuing drama about the lives and relationships of recurring characters.

items.pt: reality show; programa de televisão de realidade
items.example: The reality TV show follows people sharing a house.
items.note: A programme that follows real participants through situations or challenges.

items.example: Several celebrities joined the programme.
items.note: A person who is widely known, especially through media and entertainment.

items.example: The guest is a well-known musician.
items.note: An adjective meaning famous or widely recognised; usually hyphenated before a noun.

items.example: Which channel is showing the match?
items.note: Normally used for a television broadcasting service; contrast radio station.

items.pt: estação de rádio; emissora de rádio
items.example: What radio station do you listen to?
items.note: Commonly used for a radio broadcasting service; contrast TV channel.

items.example: Members discuss local issues in an online forum.
items.note: A place on a website where people exchange opinions or messages.

items.example: You can leave a message in the discussion forum.
items.note: Leave means post or write a message for others to read or hear.

items.example: Readers can discuss topics in the newspaper's forum.
items.note: Discuss takes a direct object; do not add about immediately after discuss.

items.pt: podcast; programa de áudio sob demanda
items.example: I listened to a podcast about science.
items.note: An audio programme that can be downloaded and played on a computer or phone.

items.example: According to the report, the train was delayed.
items.note: Introduces the source of information or a stated view.

items.pt: está escrito no jornal; o jornal diz
items.example: It says in the paper that prices may rise.
items.note: Idiomatic way to refer to printed news; not it is written in the paper in this source pattern.

items.example: According to the news, the roads will reopen today.
items.note: A way to name a news broadcast as the source of information.

items.example: Journalists report the news on radio and television.
items.note: Report can also be a verb meaning give information publicly.

sectionsChecked: A: Newspapers; publishing schedules, types and digital forms
B: Contents of newspapers; reports, articles, headlines, reviews and adverts
C: Television; programme types, celebrities and TV channel versus radio station
D: Media reporting; forums, podcasts and reporting phrases, with common-mistake note
Exercises 52.1–52.5 and Unit 52 answer key; TV programme types, crossword and sentence completions
